name: Bell 47
summary: Iconic early piston helicopter with a goldfish-bowl canopy and open truss tail boom, still flown for crop spraying, sightseeing and as a warbird.

wings: Two-blade main rotor with a weighted stabilizer bar crossing below the blades
engines: Exposed piston engine mounted upright behind the cabin
47G: two saddle fuel tanks on either side above the engine
fuselage: Skids, often with spray booms on ag aircraft
tail: Small two-blade tail rotor with a tubular guard below it

tellTales: Open lattice framework tail boom you can see through
Exposed upright engine with saddle tanks behind the canopy

confusedWith.howToTell: The Schweizer/Hughes 300 has a three-blade rotor and an enclosed tubular boom held by struts; the Bell 47 has two blades and an open lattice boom.
The R22 has an enclosed tubular tail boom and a small pointed cabin; the Bell 47 has an open truss boom and a round fishbowl canopy.

usCount.source: FAA registry make/model inquiry (Bell 47 series, all registered examples)
